CORROSION RESISTANCE OF 28%CR
DUPLEX STAINLESS STEEL TUBE
XN HOT SEAWATER APPLICATIONS
Shigeki Azuma*, Kazuhiro Ogawa*, Hideaki Miyuki*,
Takeo Kudo" and Michio Nishi**
Sumitomo Metal Industries, Ltd.
* Iron & Steel Research Laboratories, Amagasaki, Japan
** Specialty Tubing Technology Section, Head Office, Tokyo, Japan
Synopsis: A new duplex stainless steel containing
was developed. The tube
of the duplex stainless steel was manufactured by a powder metallurgical process which was
introduced to avoid the sigma-emblittlement of the billet. The developed steel was
superior to a conventional 25%Cr duplex stainless steel and equalto super-ferritic or
super-austenitic stainless steels on the resistance to pitting and crevice corrosion in hot
seawater environments. Further, the corrosion resistance of the weldment was investigated
and the effect of the welding procedure was clarified. Consequently, the developed steel
was considered to be suitable for hot seawater applications such as heat exchanger tube.

Key words: duplex stainless steel, super-stainless steel, powder metallurgy, pitting
corrosion, crevice corrosion, seawater, heat exchanger tube
1. Introduction
Ferritic-austenitic duplex stainless steels(SSs) have been used as the tubular
products in chemical industries, for example, heat exchanger tubes and various pipings [1]-
[3]. They are superior to ferritic SSs in toughness and weldability, and to austenitic SSs
in stress corrosion cracking resistance. Duplex SSs have another advantage over austenitic
SSs in cost saving, because they need less Ni content than austenitic SSs when their
contents of Cr and Mo are increased for improving the corrosion resistance. For this
reason, duplex SSs of high Cr and Mo contents have been applied to severely corrosive
environments as a substitute for expensive austenitic SSs.
Recently, ferritic and austenitic SSs which are called 'super-SSs' have been
developed for the application in the highly corrosive environments containing chloride ion
such as seawater [4]-[8]. They contain more Cr, Mo (and N for super-austenitic SSs) as
alloying elements than conventional SSs to improve the corrosion resistance. On the other
hand the commercial duplex SSs, in general, contain less Cr and Mo than the super-SSs, and
do not always have enough corrosion resistance on the hot seawater application [3]. It is
thought to be worthwhile to develop a super-duplex SS which contains high Cr and Mo and has
the corrosion resistance equal to super-ferritic and austenitic SSs[9]. As for duplex SSs,
however, the increase in the Cr and Mo contents for improving the corrosion resistance
accelerates the sigma phase precipitation to bring the embrittlement of the billet on tube
making process. This is the reason why the super-duplex SS has been difficult to
manufacture by the conventional process.
In this report a new duplex SS containing 28%Cr and 3.8%Mo is introduced which has
been developed by applying a powder metallurgical method by which the sigma-embrittlement
of the billet can be avoided.The corrosion resistance of the developed steel including
its weldment is also presented on the application in hot seawater environment.

2. Development of 28%Cr duplex stainless steel
2-1. Background
The addition of Cr and Mo is necessary to improve the resistance to the localized
corrosion by chloride attack. When a index, which is called pitting index(P. I.) and
calculated by (%Cr) + 3(%Mo) + 10(%N), is introduced to estimate the resistance to pitting
corrosion of SSs, some typical super-SSs proves to have the P. I. value over 40 [5],[10].
On the other hand the conventional duplex SS containing 25%Cr and 3%Mo only have the P. I.
value around 36. Therefore a super-duplex SS with the corrosion resistance equal to super-
ferritic and austenitic SSs is necessary to contain much higher contents of Cr and Mo.
However the duplex SS tube of higher Cr and Mo contents cannot be easily manufactured by
the usual process because the sigma-emblittlement of the billet becomes a serious
problem.
To avoid the sigma-emblittlement problem a
powder metallurgical(P/M) technique was
introduced to the tube manufacturing process.
In the P/M process the billet consists of the
powder which is packed in a steel capsule and
consequently no sigma-emblittlement occurs.

decided to be 27.5%Cr-7%Ni-3.8%Mo-0.3%N.
2-3. Tube manufacturing
The seamless tube of the 28%Cr duplex SS with the optimum chemical composition was
manufactured through the P/M process shown in Fig. 6 [14]. The duplex SS powder was atom-
ized by nitrogen gas and packed into a mild steel capsule. The powder billet was processed
by cold isostatic pressing(CIP) and hot extruded to the tube. The tube was acid pickled in
order to remove the capsule and then heat treated at 1373K(1100°C) followed by water
quenching.

Crevice corrosion is more important
problem than pitting corrosion for SSs
because the former occurs more frequently
than the latter in chloride containing
environments such as seawater. The crevice
corrosion potential of the all materials
became less noble than the pitting poten-

gave the following rank on the crevice
corrosion resistance: 25%Cr duplex SS <
super-austenitic SS(254) < 28%Cr duplex SS
< super-ferritic SS(2942) which indicates
that the ferritic SS is more resistant to
crevice corrosion than the austenitic one
even with the same P. I. value in contrast
to the .pitting corrosion resistance shown
in Fig. 8 [5], [15]. Fig. 9 shows the
effect of temperature and chloride concen-
tration on the crevice corrosion behavior
of the alloys by the constant potential
test at 0.4V in NaCl solutions for 48h.
The difference in the critical chloride
concentration among the alloys was consist-
ent with the rank obtained from the crevice
corrosion potential in Fig. 8. The 28%Cr
duplex SS and the super-ferritic SS were
the most resistant to crevice corrosion.
The 28%Cr duplex SS showed a good corrosion
resistance in the immersion test for 6
months in the actual seawater; it suffered
no crevice corrosion.

content of the 25%Cr duplex SS increased
with increasing temperature to reach about

ferrite content of the 28%Cr duplex SS
did not change so much; it was still
only 65% after 1623K(1350°C) heating.
That is attributed to the rapid auste-
nite phase formation during the cooling
on the 28%Cr duplex SS which contains
high N of 0.3%. Nitrogen atom is the
potential element for stabilizing the
austenitic phase and diffuses more
rapidly than the metal element atoms
such as Ni, Cr and Mo. Although the
pitting potentials of the both duplex
SSs were decreased in the same manner,
the 28%Cr duplex SS after 1623K(1350°C)
heating was still more resistant to
pitting corrosion than the 25%Cr duplex
SS's base metal.

on the 28%Cr duplex SS which contains
high N of 0.3%. Nitrogen atom is the
potential element for stabilizing the
austenitic phase and diffuses more
rapidly than the metal element atoms
such as Ni, Cr and Mo. Although the
pitting potentials of the both duplex
SSs were decreased in the same manner,
the 28%Cr duplex SS after 1623K(1350°C)
heating was still more resistant to
pitting corrosion than the 25%Cr duplex
SS's base metal.
The corrosion resistance of the
welded joint was investigated to clarify
the effect of the welding procedure.
Firstly, the girth welding was performed
by GTAW with the heat input of 6 to
13.5kJ/cm using the similar filler metal
to the 28%Cr duplex SS. The results are
shown in Fig. 11 where the pitting
potential is plotted against the heat
input. The pitting potential decreased
with increasing heat input. However
even when the heat input was 12kJ/cm,
the pitting potential was about 0.5V vs
SCE and still higher than that of the
25%Cr duplex SS's base metal.

4. Conclusions
Fig.13 Pitting potential of tube-to-
tube sheet weldment
1) A super-duplex stainless steel which was composed of 27.5%Cr-7%Ni-3.8%Mo-0.3%N was
developed from the investigation of the weldment performance. The seamless tube of the
alloy was successfully manufactured by the powder metallurgical process.
2) The corrosion resistance of the 28%Cr duplex SS in hot seawater environments was
superior to the conventional 25%Cr duplex SS and almost equal to those of super-ferritic
and super-austenitic stainless steels.
3) The 25%Cr duplex SS was found to be applicable as the tube sheet material matching with
the 28%Cr duplex SS tube from the viewpoint of the pitting corrosion resistance of the seal
weldment.
4) The developed alloy was concluded to be suitable for the application in the highly
corrosive environments such as hot seawater.
